note: Only one source family prints the true point in a readable form: Wikidata gives 51°9'12.960"N, 3°27'28.908"W (NHLE-referenced), matching the Exmoor HER grid reference SS 9811 4037 and Geograph's photo of the enclosure (51:9.2091N 3:27.4941W), i.e. about 51.1535, -3.4582. The stored point, copied from the English Wikipedia infobox, lies about 1.75 km too far north near Bat's Castle, but no second independent source prints decimal or DMS coordinates, so it is held for the owner.

Only the Wikipedia family (the French site article and its Wikidata item, 46°39'0"N 6°32'13"E) prints a point for the archaeological site; the excavators' chronicle (ArcheoBase) gives only a Swiss grid reference (2530800/1167610, near the stored point), and no second independent source printing latitude/longitude for the site could be found.

Only the Wikipedia family prints a point for the ruins (14.86611, 39.42389, about 1.4 km south of the stored point); Pleiades (representative point about 14.8688, 39.4229) is behind a bot wall, the UNESCO tentative list is unreadable, and the aggregator pages copy either Wikidata or the stored point, so no second independent quotable source exists and the point is held for the owner.

The stored point is the centre of Shewaki village, about 6 km west of the stupa. The stupa's own point is given only by the conservators' monograph (ACHCO: 34°26'N 69°17'E) and by OpenStreetMap (Shewaki Stupa at 34.44102, 69.28136, where satellite imagery shows the restored stupa), whose page prints latitude and longitude separately in a form the check cannot read, so no two quotable independent sources exist; held for the owner with 34.44102, 69.28136 as the likely point.

Magh Slécht is a historic plain of about 8 km2 in Templeport parish holding over 80 monuments; only Wikipedia and its Wikidata item (one source family, a rounded 54.08, -7.66) give a point for it, and no independent source gives a point for the plain itself, so the point is held for the owner.

Only the Wikipedia/Wikidata family prints a point (13°45′59″S 73°48′08″W, 0.15 km from the stored point); the MINCETUR inventory (copied on Turismo Peruano) places the ruins only in the annex of Rayme Alto, 2.5 km south of Carhuanca at 3,267 m, and GeoNames and OpenStreetMap have no record, so no second independent point can be quoted.

The entry is the whole underground geothermal zone and tunnel network beneath Naples, running from Vesuvius through Pompeii and Herculaneum and the Campi Flegrei to Pozzuoli and Baia, which is an area and not a single monument; the English Wikipedia article prints no coordinates, and the only point tied to the Wikidata item (40.851044, 14.256867, Piazza San Gaetano) belongs to the Napoli Sotterranea visitor museum, a different object 2 km from the stored point. No two independent sources give a point for the site itself, so the stored point stays held for the owner.

The only printed point for the Bahşeyiş monument is the Wikidata item Q134728456 (39°9'11.05"N, 30°34'30.68"E, about 70 m from the stored point), which is an import of Kültür Envanteri; Phrygian Monuments, the Eskişehir directorate and the TAY project describe its place (1 km SW of Gökbahçe, west bank of the Kocadere) but give no coordinates, so no second independent source can be quoted.

The Icknield Way is a braided trackway 'from Norfolk to Wiltshire' (Wikipedia); the stored point is Lyme Regis in Dorset, the far end of the modern Greater Ridgeway and not on the Icknield Way itself, but neither Wikipedia nor any other source prints one point for the whole route (Wikidata carries an unsourced point near Ivinghoe), so no two independent sources can be quoted for the site's point.

Only the Wikipedia family (the English article's infobox, 55.81003389, 10.62370472, about 13 m from the stored point, and its Wikidata item) prints a point for the site; the national register Fund og Fortidsminder holds the locality Tønnesminde (030505-96) but prints no coordinates, so no second independent source can be quoted.

The entry names the municipality of Gilching and its stored point is the town centre (the municipality's article coordinates). The prehistoric barrows it stands for are scattered over the municipal area (west of Rottenried, Baderwinkel, south of the Wildmoos, Strahlenholz near Geisenbrunn, and the forest towards Schöngeising), and no source gives one point for them, so the site's point cannot be sourced.

The entry is the Early Bronze Age mound fields of the Cetina culture, which the sources place at several locations along the Cetina valley (around Cetina, Vrlika and Bajagic), not at one point; the stored point is the river's mouth at Omis from the river article and the Wikidata point is the river's source, and no source gives a point for the site itself.

Only Wikidata (38.481899, 22.50154, the same family as the Wikipedia article) prints a point for the Cnidian Treasury in a quotable form. OpenStreetMap's node is shown only by Mapcarta, in a form the checker cannot read ('38.48186° or 38° 28′ 55″ north'), and trek.zone is an unattributed aggregator. No second reputable, independent source can be quoted, although every point found lies within about 70 m of the stored one.

Pleiades lists Prosymna as unlocated (Barrington Atlas 'unlocated'), ToposText gives 37.68, 22.78 only with 'Confidence: Nil', rounding the English Wikipedia point 37°41'N 22°47'E it links to, and Wikidata puts it 1.4 km away near the Argive Heraion; there are no two independent, reliable sources for the town's point.

Only Wikipedia gives a readable point (18°19′N 88°30′W, for the village, within 0.1 km of the stored point); the excavation report's datum is printed in a garbled OCR form that cannot be read as a point, and GeoNames/Mapcarta put a 'Louisville' ruin 9 km east, contradicting the excavators' location beside the Northern Highway; with no second independent source the point is held for the owner.

The site is the pre-Hispanic cemetery with a shaft tomb that INAH excavated in 2013 'al oriente de la ciudad de Colima'. No source gives its exact position. The only printed point, the Megalithic Portal's 19.24 N 103.724 W, is the centre of Colima city ('Nearest Town: Colima'), and the Wikidata item is the state of Colima, not the site.

The site is the 2008 warrior grave at Bersted Park, North Bersted near Bognor Regis; the stored point lies in Chichester at the Novium Museum that keeps the finds, about 8 km away. No readable source prints coordinates for the grave itself, so the point is held for the owner.

The only coordinates published for the find site are English Wikipedia's and Wikidata's 42°05′N 42°05′E, which are the rounded coordinates of Shukhuti village itself (the village article carries the same point). The excavated bath lay on M. Khalvashi's plot in the village, but no second independent source gives a point for it, so the point is held for the owner.

The site is the lost Tan Hill white horse (the 'Tan Hill Donkey'), not the hill. Wiltshire White Horses and the Hillfigure Homepage place it only by the grid reference SU 080 644 (roughly 0.25 km south-west of the stored summit point), and Wikipedia's coordinates are the hill summit's; no two sources print the figure's own point in degrees.

The MINCETUR inventory record (as reproduced by turismoperuano.com) gives the complex as UTM 8 181 271 N / 763 804 E at 227 m, i.e. about -16.4356, -72.5296 beside the hamlet of Huamboy and the Huamboy cliffs (GeoNames -16.4333, -72.5167) in Nicolás de Piérola District, some 25 km north-east of the stored point, which only matches the Wikidata mountain item; a UTM reference is not read and no two independent sources print the site's point in degrees, so the point is held for the owner.

The stored point lies about 10 m from the Chapel of Osiris Heqadjet in East Karnak (Wikidata Q124824888 gives 25.71785, 32.6611; the Precinct of Amun-Re article lists it as 'Chapel of Osiris / Heqadjet'), but only the Wikimedia family prints a point for it, so no second independent source can be quoted. Note for the owner: the stored source article describes a different chapel, Osiris-Ptah Neb-ankh, about 0.55 km south-west by the Tenth Pylon.

The Wikidata/Wikipedia point (40.16389, 45.57222) and GeoNames' points are the village of Karchaghbyur and its stream, not the archaeological site; the site itself (per Kiesling's Rediscovering Armenia, a Persian and Hellenistic walled settlement on a promontory jutting into Lake Sevan, with nearby graves) has no published point that two independent sources print.

No source prints a point for a Trypillia settlement at Ksaverove: the only pages that mention one are copies of an English Wikipedia article deleted on 2026-01-29 (WP:CSD G12, its cited source did not mention the claim) and a Wikipedia list without coordinates, and the stored point (49.1946, 31.5181) lies at the village, which is not the site.
